E_linear_trend_kp.description: Use only delta_kp_index (t5 - t0). Threshold=0.3 is POST-HOC OPTIMISED on test set — upper bound only, not a generalisation result.

F_multi_feature_threshold.description: kp_index_t5 > 4.0 OR delta_kp_index > 1.0. Fixed thresholds, not tuned.

G_always_critical.description: Always predict CRITICAL_AHEAD. Upper bound on CRITICAL recall.

H_always_nominal.description: Always predict NOMINAL_AHEAD. Upper bound on NOMINAL precision.

scientific_conclusion: Frozen GB macro-F1: 0.9708.  KP-only macro-F1: 0.8977.  Gap: +0.0731. Multi-feature threshold (kp_t5>4 OR delta_kp>1): macro-F1=0.9045.  Gap vs GB: 0.0663. Linear-trend KP (post-hoc optimal threshold=0.3): macro-F1=0.6715.  Gap vs GB: 0.2993. Even post-hoc optimised delta_kp alone (0.6715 macro-F1) is 0.2993 below the full GB temporal model. This gap reflects information from non-KP delta features and the full 6-step window pattern. CRITICAL_recall gap: GB=0.9819 vs KP-only=0.8382 (+0.1437). For safety-critical missed-anomaly cost, the temporal window provides a substantial and reproducible uplift over single-feature shortcuts. HONEST ASSESSMENT: The temporal window does add measurable value beyond KP-only. The +0.0731 macro-F1 and +0.1437 CRITICAL recall gains are reproducible on the frozen test set. The primary benefit is reduced missed anomalies. However, all evidence is on simulation data — the same conclusion may not hold on real spacecraft telemetry.
